title: Authored building template
description: A footprint the generator stamps onto a district, per docs/24's "authored templates, procedurally assembled". Godot-only: the frozen TypeScript oracle's CONTENT_TYPES never lists it, so this schema is read by content_validator.gd alone. Coordinates inside a template are relative to its own top-left corner -- the generator chooses the origin, so nothing in here may name an absolute district tile.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. Permanent once shipped.

name.description: What the place is called out loud. Prose, not an enum.

size.description: Footprint in tiles. Three is the smallest shell with an interior.

tiles.description: Row-major tile enums matching SimTileMap.Tile, length w*h.

doors.description: Size-relative tiles where the shell opens. At least one: a sealed footprint is a wall, not a building.

tags.description: What the placer selects on ("residential", "civic", "corner"). Free text rather than an enum while the district types are still being authored.

weight.description: Relative draw weight within a district type's pool.

roof.description: Roof material. The name resolves through content/dressing/street.json's `roofs` table to the sprite keys the renderer blits -- presentation/roof_look.gd decides cap vs face per tile and which interior tiles take a roof. A material with no table entry draws the procedural wall, which is the supported fallback.

wall.description: Wall material. The name resolves through content/dressing/street.json's `walls` table to the sprite keys the renderer blits -- presentation/roof_look.gd decides cap vs face per tile and which interior tiles take a roof. A material with no table entry draws the procedural wall, which is the supported fallback.

look.description: How this building looks: `{roof, wall}` material names that content/dressing/street.json's `roofs`/`walls` tables resolve to sprite keys. The Godot validator is shallow -- it accepts any object satisfying the top-level required/type check here and never re-checks the enum below at load -- so check_roof_look.gd's LOOK lane is what actually enforces `roof`/`wall` against the enum on every shipped template.

anchors.description: Size-relative points SimTemplates.stamp converts to absolute and writes onto the map object. Only the colony template carries these; an ordinary house has none.

tile.description: Size-relative, unlike map.schema.json's loot sites, which are absolute district tiles.

table.description: The location loot table this site rolls, matching a content/loot entry's `location`. Copied from map.schema.json and kept in step with it by hand -- LOCATIONS in check_loot.gd is what asserts nothing names a table nobody wrote.

container.description: When present the site stands as a searchable container holding the same table rather than being scattered at boot. Prose read only by SimContainers.hud_clause.
